zh: 或者给他们更多的推理能力来运行测试。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's funny, I think you guys as being security practitioners, you've had a number of calls with people that want to talk to you about, how can I secure my company?
zh: 很有趣，我认为你们作为安全从业者，你们已经接到过很多人的电话，想和你讨论如何保护我的公司？

speaker: Unknown
en: How can I secure my business?
zh: 如何保护我的业务？

speaker: Unknown
en: How can I secure my product?
zh: 如何保护我的产品？

speaker: Unknown
en: And those conversations are always some form of, I don't want to hire people or pay money for this, and how do I do it cheaply?
zh: 这些谈话总是一种形式，我不想雇人或者为此付钱，我怎么能便宜地做到这一点？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, so thank you guys for coming out to the desert.
zh: 是的，所以感谢你们来到沙漠。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're not here to see us, obviously.
zh: 显然你们不是来看我们的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're all here for Black Hat.
zh: 我们都是为了 Black Hat 而来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Would love, you know, I know that this is neither of your first times here, certainly not my first time here.
zh: 我很想,你知道,我知道这不是你们第一次来这里,当然也不是我第一次来这里。

speaker: Unknown
en: Would maybe love to get your guys' takes on what you're seeing.
zh: 也许想听听你们的看法,关于你们看到了什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's the mood like?
zh: 气氛怎么样?

speaker: Unknown
en: What's interesting?
zh: 有什么有趣的?

speaker: Unknown
en: What are the observations you've got that are catching your eyes?
zh: 你们有什么观察引起了你们的注意?

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, at least for us at Socket, I think the biggest thing we're seeing is that 2026 is the year of the software supply chain.
zh: 我的意思是,至少对于我们在 Socket 来说,我认为我们看到最大的一件事是 2026 年是软件供应链的一年。

speaker: Unknown
en: That you're dealing with an incident right now as the conference is happening.
zh: 你们在会议进行期间正在处理一个事件。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes, and I noticed the attackers seem to pick RSA and Black Hat as the times they want to start these NPM worms.
zh: 是的,我注意到攻击者似乎选择 RSA 和 Black Hat 作为他们想要启动这些 NPM 蠕虫的时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: The hacker, the security guy in the office.
zh: 那个黑客,办公室里的安全人员。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, absolutely.
zh: 是的,确实。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think that's the thing that's the biggest, you know, I think, you know, prior years, I was having to educate people.
zh: 所以我认为这是最大的事情,你知道,我认为,你知道,在过去的几年里,我不得不教育人们。

speaker: Unknown
en: We were, you know, always educating people about this problem and having to explain to them, you know, this is not a theoretical risk, like this can happen.
zh: 我们总是,你知道,在教育人们关于这个问题,不得不向他们解释,你知道,这不是一个理论上的风险,像这样可能发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we'd sometimes get these reactions like, oh, yeah, but like, how likely is it really?
zh: 我们有时会得到这些反应,比如,哦,是的,但是,像,这真的有多大可能性?

speaker: Unknown
en: And we're like, no, it's actually very likely.
zh: 我们说,不,这实际上非常可能。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let me tell you how it could happen.
zh: 让我告诉你它是如何发生的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And, you know, there were many incidents to point to, but I think...
zh: 而且,你知道,有很多事件可以指出,但我想...

speaker: Unknown
en: This year, it's really broken through into the mainstream.
zh: 今年,它真的突破了进入主流。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's like mainstream publications, you know, the business press covering these attacks, right?
zh: 有像主流出版物,你知道,商业媒体报道这些攻击,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like Storm Page on Bloomberg.
zh: 就像 Bloomberg 上的 Storm Page。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, exactly.
zh: 是的,完全正确。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think that is very, very good because you need that type of, you know, air cover for like security teams to actually prioritize and find budget for these problems.
zh: 所以我认为这是非常好的,因为你需要那种类型的,你知道,掩护,以便安全团队能够真正确定优先级并为这些问题找到预算。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think, you know, despite all these attacks being very...
zh: 所以我认为,你知道,尽管所有这些攻击都非常...

speaker: Unknown
en: We found a database credential recently that had access to 3.6% of the global PII.
zh: 我们最近发现了一个数据库凭证,它有权访问全球 3.6% 的 PII。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like 3.6% of the world's population had their PII in this database.
zh: 就像全球 3.6% 的人口的 PII 都在这个数据库中。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the reason we found it is because we're partnering with organizations like Hugging Face to just get all the live credentials revoked and cleaned up better otherwise on their platforms.
zh: 我们发现它的原因是我们正在与 Hugging Face 这样的组织合作,以撤销所有实时凭证并在其平台上更好地清理。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's great to see those types of organizations leaning in.
zh: 所以很高兴看到这些类型的组织参与进来。

speaker: Unknown
en: And like all of the data that's being scraped from all these places, it creates really a central place where we can scan and make material progress.
zh: 就像从所有这些地方抓取的所有数据一样,它创造了一个中心位置,我们可以扫描并取得实质性进展。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think like when it comes to secrets, we're kind of seeing the older generation like HashiCorp got acquired, CyberArk got acquired, kind of get pushed out, which has sort of led to a new conversation about non-human identity and secrets about how can we make them easier to use, how can we get them revoked, and how can we really move the needle forward with the industry that we weren't able to do before under sort of the old guard.
zh: 所以我认为,当涉及到秘密时,我们正在看到老一代像 HashiCorp 被收购, CyberArk 被收购,被挤出,这引发了一场关于非人类身份和秘密的新对话,关于我们如何让它们更容易使用,我们如何让它们被撤销,以及我们如何真正推动行业向前发展,这是我们以前在旧守卫派下无法做到的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, absolutely.
zh: 是的,绝对。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I can imagine that there's going to be a multiplication effect, which is it used to be one user with 10 passwords, and now you're going to have 10 agents with 10 passwords, right?
zh: 我可以想象会有一个倍增效应,以前是一个用户有 10 个密码,现在你将有 10 个智能体有 10 个密码,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, the way agents interact with secrets right now is a Wild West unsolved problem that we're working very hard to solve.
zh: 我的意思是,智能体目前与秘密交互的方式是一个 Wild West(西部蛮荒)未解决的问题,我们正在非常努力地解决。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of many issues.
zh: 许多问题之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you, gentlemen, for joining me.
zh: 谢谢你们加入我。

speaker: Unknown
en: This has been awesome.
zh: 这很棒。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's great to catch up.
zh: 很高兴叙旧。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thanks, Joel.
zh: 谢谢, Joel。

zh: 感谢收听 A16Z 播客的这一集。
